commit.message:
Maker Week: make firebase-apk-scanner report what the scan actually found (#374)

* fix(firebase-apk-scanner): read the current report, keep it on nonzero exit, count vulnerabilities once

- Step 3 ran `cat firebase_scan_*/scan_report.txt`, which also reads every
  earlier scan in the directory, and took counts from the text report
  although the reporting rule names scan_report.json. Read the JSON (and
  text) report in the directory the scanner printed as `Results saved to:`.
- scanner.sh exits 1 after writing its report when no APK could be tested,
  which the "if the scanner fails" fallback read as a failure and started
  manual live probes. Present a written report on any exit code; fall back
  only when no report exists.
- State the scanner's coverage limits (Cloud Functions in us-central1 only;
  auth, functions and Remote Config for the first project and key only).
- The per-APK "APK IS VULNERABLE" summary line used log_vuln, which counts
  toward TOTAL_VULNS, so total_vulnerabilities was one too high for every
  vulnerable APK. Log it with log_error. Documented output change.
- Quote "$ARGUMENTS" so paths with spaces work.

tests/test_scanner_reports.py runs the scanner with mocked apktool and curl
(secure, vulnerable, no-config, failed) and checks the counts, the stale
directory, and the SKILL.md guidance; two tests fail before this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(firebase-apk-scanner): load the manual-testing fallback only when needed

Move "Manual Testing (If Scanner Fails)" word for word into
references/manual-fallback.md and leave a two-line pointer: it is only
needed when the scanner wrote no report, but every run loaded it. Every
other section is unchanged. Bump firebase-apk-scanner to 2.2.3.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
